claims.text: Partial charge transfer among constituent metals is a key determinant of uniform single-phase formation in noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
Partial charge transfer stabilizes a homogeneous alloy structure.
Charge transfer electronically modulates noble-metal active sites and thereby enhances catalytic performance.
Near-equiatomic Pt, Pd, and Au together with Ni, Co, and Cu are suitable precursor constituents for the proposed one-pot synthesis.
Multi-edge in situ X-ray absorption and scattering measurements can track metal oxidation states and alloy formation during synthesis.
Local partial charge redistribution among co-reduced metals facilitates homogeneous alloying into a single-phase high-entropy structure.
Partial charge transfer lowers reaction-energy barriers during precursor reduction and nucleation.
Partial charge transfer promotes uniform elemental distribution in emerging nanoparticles.
Uniform alloying optimizes the metallic bonding environment and active-site electronic structure.
The proposed high-entropy synthesis will produce earlier and more synchronous transitions to metallic states for all constituent elements.
Consistent narrowing of interatomic distances in EXAFS is an indicator of homogeneous alloying.
The resulting high-entropy alloy will have higher catalytic turnover rates than reference bimetallic materials or products of non-synchronous synthesis.
An otherwise identical bimetallic synthesis will exhibit less partial charge redistribution.
Less partial charge redistribution in the bimetallic baseline will cause phase segregation or uneven alloying.
The bimetallic baseline will have lower catalytic activity than the high-entropy alloy.
The hypothesis applies when synthesis temperatures permit sufficient precursor reduction and mobility.
Excessively high synthesis temperatures can cause rapid particle growth or sintering and therefore define an upper boundary for the hypothesis.
Highly disparate reduction potentials can disrupt the proposed relationship between charge transfer and homogeneous alloying.
Large atomic-size mismatches can disrupt the proposed relationship between charge transfer and homogeneous alloying.
